args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks – rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api v2.3.1 (latest production deploy) was failing health checks in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an 18% error rate. Rolled back all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. Post-rollback: service healthy, error rate 0.2%. Note: v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging prior to the production deploy. Follow-up: root-cause the v2.3.1 regression and review why it was promoted despite failing in staging.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened a SEV2 incident, which paged the on-call engineer.

- **Problem:** The latest deploy, v2.3.1, was failing health checks in us-east, us-west and eu-west, with an 18% error rate.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 is the most recent version that was healthy in production. All three regions now run it, the service passes health checks and the error rate is down to 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 (SEV2, checkout-api) describes the failure, the rollback and the recovery.

The release history shows v2.3.1 was also failing in staging before it went to production. I noted that in the incident and suggested two follow-ups: find the root cause of the failure, and check why the release was pushed to production anyway.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
